subject: english
title: Word Twins Review
objective: Identify synonyms and antonyms by comparing word meanings.
introduction: Milo compares word cards about feelings, actions, temperature, and time. Can you tell whether each pair has a similar or opposite meaning?

vocabulary.definition: a pair whose words name nearly the same idea
a pair whose words both describe starting an action
a pair whose words point in opposite directions

activities.instruction: Read each pair and compare the ideas the words name.
activities.content: Synonyms have similar meanings; antonyms have opposite meanings.

feedback.retry: Compare both meanings again before naming the relationship.

activities.prompt: Learn how synonyms share meaning and antonyms show opposites.
activities.narration: Synonyms have similar meanings; antonyms have opposite meanings. Compare the ideas, not just the spelling.
activities.guideHint: Ask whether the words match or point in opposite directions.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Synonyms have similar meanings; antonyms have opposite meanings. Compare the ideas, not just the spelling.

activities.instruction: Tap pairs whose meanings match or oppose each other.

feedback.retry: Check whether the pair is similar or opposite.

activities.prompt: Find word pairs with a clear meaning relationship.
activities.narration: Happy and glad share a meaning; hot and cold show opposites.
activities.guideHint: Say what each word means before comparing them.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Happy and glad share a meaning; hot and cold show opposites.

activities.instruction: Sort related word pairs from unrelated pairs.

feedback.retry: Name the relationship before sorting again.

activities.prompt: Sort each pair by whether its meanings connect clearly.
activities.narration: A related pair has a same-meaning or opposite-meaning rule; an unrelated pair does not.
activities.guideHint: Try to state the relationship between the two meanings.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: A related pair has a same-meaning or opposite-meaning rule; an unrelated pair does not.

activities.instruction: Tap the pair with the requested meaning relationship.

feedback.retry: Look for two words that name nearly the same idea.

activities.prompt: Choose the pair whose words share a meaning.
activities.narration: Synonyms name nearly the same idea, so happy and glad belong together.
activities.guideHint: Say what both words mean and compare.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Synonyms name nearly the same idea, so happy and glad belong together.

activities.instruction: Match each word pair to the rule it shows.

feedback.retry: Check whether the two ideas match or oppose.

activities.prompt: Match each pair with its meaning relationship.
activities.narration: The rule explains whether the pair shares an idea or shows an opposite.
activities.guideHint: Read both words, then choose the same-meaning or opposite-meaning rule.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: The rule explains whether the pair shares an idea or shows an opposite.

activities.instruction: Put the word-comparing steps in order.

feedback.retry: Check that you read, compared, named, and explained.

activities.prompt: Order the steps for comparing two word meanings.
activities.narration: Readers compare each word’s idea before naming the relationship.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Readers compare each word’s idea before naming the relationship.

items.prompt: After good news, Ana feels happy. Which pair gives the same meaning?
items.explanation: Happy and glad both describe feeling good, so they are synonyms.

items.prompt: A sign says begin the game, and another says start the game. Which pair matches?
items.explanation: Begin and start both tell someone to get an action going, so their meanings match.

items.prompt: Milo drinks hot cocoa and eats cold ice. Which pair shows opposites?
items.explanation: Hot and cold point in opposite directions on temperature.

items.prompt: The bell rings early, but the bus arrives late. Which pair are antonyms?
items.explanation: Early means before a time and late means after it, so they are opposites.

items.prompt: Jo feels happy after a win. Which pair has the same meaning?
items.explanation: Happy and glad both name a good feeling, so they are synonyms.
